location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
location.notes: Refers to home universities of participants, not travel destination.

control.notes: Study design is a before/after travel cohort, not a case-control design; no explicit control group designation.

fmt_id.notes: Not applicable; not an FMT study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Not applicable; adult travelers, not neonates.

extraction_warnings: Individual subject/sample identifiers, exact ages, and per-subject metadata are only available in supplementary Table S1 and Table S2, which were not provided in the text; only cohort-level aggregates could be extracted.

Granularity was classified as subgroup_level (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) because some fields (e.g., subject counts, antimalarial use, ESBL acquisition) are stratified by destination, while others (e.g., age range, sex ratio, antibiotics use) are reported only at the whole-cohort level.
Sex and antibiotic use percentages are cohort-level aggregates, not individual-level values; these were not snapped to single enum values per the extraction rules.
Most schema fields (disease staging, oncology response, neonatal, obgyn, HLA, smoker) are not applicable to this traveler/microbiome study and were marked not_reported.

Granularity is mixed: overall cohort-level resistance gene fold-changes are study-level, while ESBL acquisition and diarrhea prevalence are explicitly stratified by travel destination (subgroup_level); this paper was classified as subgroup_level overall to capture the destination-specific ESBL finding, but many fields apply only at study_level.
Treatment field repurposed to capture antimalarial chemoprophylaxis usage since no therapeutic treatment was administered in this observational travel study.
